precepts.text: Asa rested on the Lord against a thousand thousand Ethiopians; it is nothing with the Lord to help, whether with many or with them that have no power.
precepts.point: The victory of battle stands not in the multitude of an host; strength comes from heaven. Whether with many or with them that have no power, the battle is not yours but God's; our forefathers proved it, as when Asa cried to the Lord and a million Ethiopians fell before Judah and Benjamin.

note.label: Genesis 14: The War of the Kings and Melchizedek

precepts.why:
Our forefathers proved that strength comes from heaven. Zerah the Ethiopian came out against Asa “with an host of a thousand thousand, and three hundred chariots”, a million men. Asa set the battle in array and cried unto the Lord his God: “Lord, it is nothing with thee to help, whether with many, or with them that have no power: help us, O Lord our God; for we rest on thee, and in thy name we go against this multitude.”

A million Ethiopians fell before Judah and Benjamin. It is nothing with the Lord to help, whether with many or with them that have no power.

That is the same Lord Abram rested on when he took three hundred and eighteen men and three confederates against four kingdoms and smote them by night. The victory of battle stands not in the multitude of an host; “let not man prevail against thee.”

precepts.text: Asa cried unto the Lord, It is nothing with thee to help, whether with many, or with them that have no power: help us, O Lord our God, for we rest on thee, and in thy name we go against this multitude; that is the faith you see in Jonathan and this young servant, two men going against an army in the name of the Lord.
precepts.point: The Lord put that spirit on Jonathan. That is how the Most High operates: he loves to show his power by having a small number defeat a very large number. That is why it will be the 144,000 taking over the whole world; that is just how he rolls.

note.label: 1 Samuel 14: By Many or by Few

precepts.why:
Asa had the same faith: “Lord, it is nothing with thee to help, whether with many, or with them that have no power: help us, O Lord our God; for we rest on thee, and in thy name we go against this multitude. O Lord, thou art our God; let not man prevail against thee.”

That is the faith you see in Jonathan and this young servant: “there is no restraint to the Lord to save by many or by few.” Two men going against an army in the name of the Lord.

precepts.text: For three years they walked in the way of David and Solomon and strengthened the kingdom of Judah.
precepts.point: Asa commands Judah to seek the Most High and to do the law and the commandment. The pattern of Rehoboam warns what happens when a strong king forsakes that law.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 14: Asa Seeks the Most High and Finds Rest

precepts.why:
“So they strengthened the kingdom of Judah, and made Rehoboam the son of Solomon strong, three years: for three years they walked in the way of David and Solomon.”

Walking in the way of David and Solomon is what strengthens the kingdom. Asa walked that way: he “did that which was good and right in the eyes of the Lord his God”, took away the altars of the strange gods, the high places, the images and the groves, and “commanded Judah to seek the Lord God of their fathers, and to do the law and the commandment.” And “the kingdom was quiet before him.”

precepts.text: When Rehoboam had established the kingdom and strengthened himself, he forsook the law of the Lord, and all Israel with him.
precepts.point: Asa commands Judah to seek the Most High and to do the law and the commandment. The pattern of Rehoboam warns what happens when a strong king forsakes that law.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 14: Asa Seeks the Most High and Finds Rest

precepts.why:
“And it came to pass, when Rehoboam had established the kingdom, and had strengthened himself, he forsook the law of the Lord, and all Israel with him.”

The pattern of Rehoboam warns what happens when a strong king forsakes that law. Asa did the opposite: he commanded Judah “to do the law and the commandment”, and “In his days the land was quiet ten years.”

precepts.text: The suburbs of the Levites' cities reach from the wall outward a thousand cubits round about, for the cities have walls.
precepts.point: Asa has an army of 300,000 of Judah and 280,000 of Benjamin, all mighty men of valor.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 14: Asa Seeks the Most High and Finds Rest

precepts.why:
“And the suburbs of the cities, which ye shall give unto the Levites, shall reach from the wall of the city and outward a thousand cubits round about.”

The law measures from the wall of the city, for the cities of Israel have walls. So Asa built fenced cities: “Let us build these cities, and make about them walls, and towers, gates, and bars, while the land is yet before us.”

precepts.text: A curse on the seed is the enemy besieging the gates until the high and fenced walls come down wherein they trusted.
precepts.point: Asa has an army of 300,000 of Judah and 280,000 of Benjamin, all mighty men of valor.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 14: Asa Seeks the Most High and Finds Rest

precepts.why:
“And he shall besiege thee in all thy gates, until thy high and fenced walls come down, wherein thou trustedst, throughout all thy land.”

That is a curse on the seed: the enemy besieging the gates until the high and fenced walls come down. Asa's day was the other side of it. “because we have sought the Lord our God, we have sought him, and he hath given us rest on every side.” So the walls went up, “So they built and prospered”, and Asa had an army of 300,000 out of Judah and 280,000 out of Benjamin, “all these were mighty men of valour.”

precepts.text: By much slothfulness the building decayeth, so the rest from war was spent building up, not idling.
precepts.point: Asa has an army of 300,000 of Judah and 280,000 of Benjamin, all mighty men of valor.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 14: Asa Seeks the Most High and Finds Rest

precepts.why:
“By much slothfulness the building decayeth; and through idleness of the hands the house droppeth through.”

Rest is not idleness. Asa “had no war in those years; because the Lord had given him rest”, and he spent that rest building up, not idling: walls, towers, gates, and bars, “while the land is yet before us.” “So they built and prospered.”

precepts.text: Elisha's servant sees the mountain full of horses and chariots of fire, for they that be with us are more than they that be with them.
precepts.point: The Most High smites the Ethiopians before Asa; they flee and are destroyed, and Judah carries away very much spoil. Faith in the Most High, not the numbers of the enemy, wins the battle.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 14: Asa Seeks the Most High and Finds Rest

precepts.why:
An host compassed the city with horses and chariots, and Elisha's servant cried, “Alas, my master! how shall we do? And he answered, Fear not: for they that be with us are more than they that be with them.” Elisha prayed, “And the Lord opened the eyes of the young man; and he saw: and, behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha.” And the Lord smote the enemy with blindness “according to the word of Elisha.”

Asa faced the same: Zerah the Ethiopian, a Cushite, came out “with an host of a thousand thousand, and three hundred chariots.” And Asa cried, “Lord, it is nothing with thee to help, whether with many, or with them that have no power.”

“So the Lord smote the Ethiopians before Asa, and before Judah; and the Ethiopians fled.” They were destroyed “before the Lord, and before his host”, and Judah carried away very much spoil. Faith in the Most High, not the numbers of the enemy, wins the battle.
